description:
Anchor redo apply's directory walks at the opened worktree-root handle, so publishing a profile no longer re-walks the absolute path from `/` down to the worktree root for each operation.

## Background

- The 45d0a971 cost harness (scenario (d)) counts directory `openat` calls of `jit profile add` for a 48-file package over four nested directories: tip 467 against base 547 (ratio 0.85, threshold ≤ 0.6). Inside the worktree the tip opens 102 directories against base 527; the tip also re-walks `/` down to the worktree root on about 73 opens (base 4), which adds about 365 at the fixture's depth. fsync: base 107 (58 directory), tip 62 (12 directory).
- Invoker ruling: the verdict counts every directory `openat` (REQ-01(d) of 45d0a971); anchor the walk at the opened worktree-root handle. Capability helpers live in `crates/jit/src/storage/capability_fs.rs` (`open_capability_parent`, `open_descendant_dir_nofollow`); redo apply in `crates/jit/src/storage/redo_apply.rs`.
- Epic criteria: `b697a3f7` REQ-14, REQ-15, REQ-22 (story `0672b087`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A redo apply opens the worktree root once and resolves every operation's parent relative to that handle; no operation re-opens an absolute path from `/`.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each parent directory is still opened and synced once per record, as `4d834432` settled; `@/inv/atomic-writes` and the symlink refusals hold unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: One test owns REQ-01 (the root is opened once per apply, observed through the existing redo-apply open-count instrumentation or its equivalent); no duplicate of 4d834432's per-parent test.
- [hard] REQ-04: Scenario (d) of the 45d0a971 harness reports tip directory opens ≤ 0.6 × base in a smoke run; the lead records the run's numbers.
title: Redo apply anchors its directory walks at the opened worktree root
